## Functions

### `applyPivot`

Apply a pivot (from `computePivotState`) to an existing view state: the
pivot's collapsed and swapped sets replace the current ones and its
`targetId` becomes the node of interest. A `null` pivot (identifier not
found) returns `vs` unchanged, same reference. Mirrors how the viewer
seeds these three fields in `buildInitialViewState`
(`tbrowse/src/store.tsx:88-96`) and how gramene-search seeds its bundle
(`Homology.js:154-161`).

```ts
function applyPivot(vs: ViewState, pivot: PivotState | null): ViewState;
```

### `buildInitialViewState`

Build the initial `ViewState` for a list of zones. Reproduces the viewer's
`buildInitialViewState` (origin `tbrowse/src/store.tsx:65-127`) with the
host data and viewer props replaced by {@link InitialViewStateOptions}:

- `zoneStates` is seeded from each zone's `defaultZoneState`, then
  `opts.zoneStates` is merged over it per zone.
- When `opts.nodeOfInterest` is given (and `opts.data` carries the tree),
  `computePivotState` supplies `collapsedNodeIds`, `swappedNodeIds` and
  `nodeOfInterestId`; an unresolvable identifier leaves them empty.
- Each zone's initial visibility is `(defaultVisible ?? true) &&
  isAvailable(data)`, with the availability check skipped (treated as
  true) when `opts.data` is omitted, then overridden by `opts.visible`,
  then subjected to the exclusive-group rule: the first qualifying member
  of a group claims it and later members start hidden.
- Each zone entry is `{ id, width: opts.widths?.[id] ?? defaultWidth, visible }`.
- `opts.overrides` is spread last, verbatim.

`rowHeight` / `fontSize` are deliberately left unset so they stay
resolvable from host props at read time.

```ts
function buildInitialViewState(zones: readonly ZoneSpec[], opts?: InitialViewStateOptions): ViewState;
```

### `computeRowRange`

Given the rows from {@link computeVisibleRows}, return the half-open index
range `[startIndex, endIndex)` of rows that intersect a scroll viewport,
padded by `overscan` rows on each side. Rows that merely touch the
viewport edge (zero-pixel intersection) are excluded. An empty row list or
a zero-height viewport yields the full range.

Origin: `tbrowse/src/layout/rowRange.ts:5-38`.

```ts
function computeRowRange(rows: VisibleRow[], scrollTop: number, viewportHeight: number, overscan?: number): RowRange;
```

### `computeVisibleRows`

Walk the tree depth-first and emit one row per visible leaf plus one
`collapsedSummary` row per collapsed internal node, assigning each row a
`y` offset so that rows pack tightly from 0. Pruned subtrees are skipped
entirely (and a collapsed node whose every leaf is pruned emits nothing);
swapped nodes have their children walked in reverse.

Origin: `tbrowse/src/visibleRows.ts:17-76`.

```ts
function computeVisibleRows(input: VisibleRowsInput): VisibleRow[];
```

### `createDerivedPruneLayer`

Build a {@link DerivedPruneLayer} for `derived`. With an empty list both
transforms return their argument unchanged (same reference), matching
`Homology.js:416-428` where the layer is bypassed entirely when there are
no genome-derived prunes.

```ts
function createDerivedPruneLayer(derived: readonly NodeId[]): DerivedPruneLayer;
```

### `decodeHashState`

Inverse of {@link encodeHashState}. Accepts the hash with or without its
leading `#`. Returns `null` for an empty hash, malformed percent-encoding
or JSON, a non-object payload, or a payload the optional type `guard`
rejects — never throws, so a bad shared link lands on a fresh view.
Origin: `main.tsx:232-244` (`decodeUrlState`).

```ts
function decodeHashState<T>(hash: string, guard?: (v: unknown) => v is T): T | null;
```

### `encodeHashState`

Serialise any JSON-able value as a URL hash: `'#' + encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify(state))`.
Origin: `main.tsx:246-248` (`encodeUrlState`).

```ts
function encodeHashState(state: unknown): string;
```

### `ensureZones`

Reconcile `vs.zones` with a zone list: entries whose id is not in `zones`
are dropped, the surviving entries keep their relative order, and a fresh
entry `{ id, width: defaultWidth, visible: defaultVisible ?? true }` is
appended for every zone that had none. `zoneStates` is left untouched.
Returns `vs` itself (same reference) when nothing needs to change.

```ts
function ensureZones(vs: ViewState, zones: readonly ZoneSpec[]): ViewState;
```

### `isViewStateLike`

Loose structural check suitable as a `decodeHashState` guard: `v` is a
non-array object and every `ViewState` field that is present has the right
container type (id lists and `zones` are arrays, `zoneStates` is an object,
`search` is `null` or an object with a string `query`). Fields may be
missing — pass the result through `normalizeViewState` to fill them.

```ts
function isViewStateLike(v: unknown): v is Partial<ViewState>;
```

### `mergeDerivedPrunes`

Union `derived` into `vs.prunedNodeIds`, keeping the user's ids first (in
their order, de-duplicated) and appending derived ids not already present
— the semantics of lodash's `_.union(user, derived)` in `Homology.js:417`.
Returns `vs` itself (same reference) when `derived` is empty, so a memo
keyed on the result stays stable while no filter is active.

```ts
function mergeDerivedPrunes(vs: ViewState, derived: readonly NodeId[]): ViewState;
```

### `normalizeViewState`

Tolerant deserialiser: turn any value — a partial state, an old persisted
blob with missing or extra fields, or garbage — into a complete
`ViewState`. Missing id arrays become `[]`, a missing or malformed `search`
becomes `null`, unknown fields are dropped, and `zoneStates` is kept as-is
(keys for unknown zones are preserved since a host-defined zone may own
them). Malformed zone entries are dropped; an entry with a non-numeric
width gets 25 and a non-boolean `visible` becomes true. When `zones` is
given the result is passed through {@link ensureZones} so every known zone
has an entry and no unknown zone does.

```ts
function normalizeViewState(input: unknown, zones?: readonly ZoneSpec[]): ViewState;
```

### `pixelWidthsToFr`

Convert target pixel widths into zone fr-shares. The viewer lays zones out
as fractions (`rendered px = width / Σwidths × container px`), so if the
shares sum to the container width, 1 fr ≈ 1 px: every zone in `targetPx`
gets its pixel target as its share and `flexZoneId` absorbs the remainder,
`max(minFlexPx, containerPx − Σ targets)`. A `targetPx` entry for the flex
zone itself is ignored. Origin:
`gramene-search/src/components/results/TaxDistTbrowse.js:180-200`.

```ts
function pixelWidthsToFr(targetPx: Record<string, number>, containerPx: number, flexZoneId: string, minFlexPx?: number): Record<string, number>;
```

### `readHashState`

Decode the current page's `location.hash` with {@link decodeHashState}.
Returns `null` when there is no `location` on `globalThis` (Node).

```ts
function readHashState<T>(guard?: (v: unknown) => v is T): T | null;
```

### `softResetForNewTree`

Reset the parts of a view state that refer to tree nodes — selection,
collapsed / pruned / swapped / compressed sets, node of interest and the
search — while keeping everything that describes the layout: `zones`,
`zoneStates`, `rowHeight`, `fontSize` and `unlinkedZoneGroups`. Use it
when the host swaps in a different tree so zone arrangement survives.
Origin: `tbrowse/examples/playground/main.tsx:836-846`
(`softResetForSourceSwitch`).

```ts
function softResetForNewTree(vs: ViewState): ViewState;
```

### `stripDerivedPrunes`

Remove every id in `derived` from `vs.prunedNodeIds`, leaving only the
user's own prunes (origin `Homology.js:420-426`). Returns `vs` itself when
`derived` is empty.

```ts
function stripDerivedPrunes(vs: ViewState, derived: readonly NodeId[]): ViewState;
```

### `stripPrunesForSnapshot`

Drop every prune from a view state about to be persisted in a snapshot:
`prunedNodeIds` becomes `[]`, everything else is copied. For hosts whose
prunes are entirely control-derived and recomputed on restore. Origin:
`gramene-search/src/bundles/viewSnapshot.js:325`.

```ts
function stripPrunesForSnapshot(vs: ViewState): ViewState;
```

### `writeHashState`

Mirror `state` into the page's URL hash via `history.replaceState`
(default, keeps the back button uncluttered) or `history.pushState`.
Skips the write when the hash already equals the encoding, and does
nothing when `globalThis` has no `location` or `history` (Node).
Origin: `main.tsx:905-925`.

```ts
function writeHashState(state: unknown, mode?: 'replace' | 'push'): void;
```

### `EMPTY_VIEW_STATE`

The all-empty view state: nothing selected, collapsed, pruned, swapped or
compressed; no node of interest; no zones; no search. Every other builder
in this module starts from it. Origin: `tbrowse/src/store.tsx:53-63`
(`baseDefaults`).

```ts
const EMPTY_VIEW_STATE: Readonly<ViewState>;
```

## Interfaces

### `DerivedPruneLayer`

A fixed set of derived prunes packaged as the two transforms a controlled
viewer needs: `effective(vs)` is what to render (user state + derived
prunes) and `onChange(next)` is what to store when the viewer reports a
change (derived prunes removed again).

```ts
interface DerivedPruneLayer {
    readonly derived: readonly NodeId[];
    effective(vs: ViewState): ViewState;
    onChange(next: ViewState): ViewState;
}
```

### `InitialViewStateOptions`

Options for {@link buildInitialViewState}.

```ts
interface InitialViewStateOptions {
    /**
     * Host data used for each zone's `isAvailable` check and for resolving
     * `nodeOfInterest` against the tree. When omitted every zone is treated as
     * available and no pivot is computed.
     */
    data?: HostData;
    /** Leaf gene id or node id to pivot the tree onto (see `computePivotState`). */
    nodeOfInterest?: string | null;
    /** Per-zone initial width (fr share), overriding `ZoneSpec.defaultWidth`. */
    widths?: Record<string, number>;
    /**
     * Per-zone initial visibility. Applied BEFORE the exclusive-group claim, so
     * forcing a zone visible lets it win its group's slot, and forcing one
     * hidden passes the slot to the next member.
     */
    visible?: Record<string, boolean>;
    /**
     * Per-zone state merged over each zone's `defaultZoneState`: a key here
     * wins over the seeded entry for that zone, and when both the seeded
     * default and the supplied value are plain objects they are shallow-merged
     * so unspecified fields keep their defaults. Zones not mentioned keep
     * their seeded defaults.
     */
    zoneStates?: Record<string, unknown>;
    /**
     * Spread LAST, verbatim, over the computed state (the `initialViewState`
     * prop of the viewer). `overrides.zoneStates` therefore REPLACES the
     * seeded map and `overrides.zones` replaces the zone list.
     */
    overrides?: Partial<ViewState>;
}
```

### `VisibleRowsInput`

Input to {@link computeVisibleRows} (origin `tbrowse/src/visibleRows.ts:6-15`).

```ts
interface VisibleRowsInput {
    tree: Tree;
    collapsedNodeIds: ReadonlySet<NodeId>;
    prunedNodeIds: ReadonlySet<NodeId>;
    /** Internal nodes whose children should be walked in reversed order. */
    swappedNodeIds?: ReadonlySet<NodeId>;
    /** Per-row height in px (leaf + collapsed-summary). Defaults to 24. */
    rowHeight?: number;
}
```
